model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral, cross-cutting way to assert that two or more identifiers denote the same subject (or a graded near-match), carrying the asserting authority, justification, confidence and temporal validity, and to project that assertion faithfully into any storage, interface or external vocabulary without silently strengthening or losing it.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 covers equivalence and near-equivalence assertions between identifiers that denote the same subject across systems, authorities and namespaces. It owns the assertion record (subject identifier, predicate/strength, object identifier, justification, asserting authority, confidence, validity), the alias-set that groups such assertions, canonical-identifier selection within an equivalence cluster, conflict/retraction/supersession records, and the platform controls that keep all of this identical across projections: namespace and prefix governance, canonical form and digests, schema versioning and patching, external predicate binding with declared downgrades, and resolution/redirect projection. It is a mixin: it attaches to any host subject model and never restates that host's own attributes or lifecycle. It aligns with external equivalence vocabularies rather than claiming conformance to them, and it references — but never implements — matching engines, access-evaluation engines, enforcement points and audit stores.
in_scope: Directed or symmetric assertions that two or more identifiers denote the same subject, each carrying its asserting authority, justification and confidence.
Graded near-equivalence (close/related match) and explicit non-equivalence assertions, qualified by the predicate and any negating modifier.
Selection and publication of a canonical or preferred identifier for an equivalence cluster, and deprecated/superseded alias status.
Alias-set level metadata: the identifier-source pair and their versions, licence, curation tooling, provider and set version.
Temporal validity of an assertion, with asserted event time kept distinct from observation and ingestion time.

Projection of an alias set into storage and interface bindings (Git-tracked file trees, MCP servers, document stores, RDF graphs, tabular exports, HTTP APIs and redirect maps) without semantic change.
Namespace ownership and prefix-to-IRI expansion governance so every compact identifier resolves deterministically without external lookup.
Canonical form, digest, patch and edition rules for alias records and alias sets.
Declared binding of internal alias strength to external equivalence predicates, with every weakening, unsupported relation kind and round-trip loss recorded.
Conflict, retraction and supersession records for contested equivalence claims, including the reciprocity status of claims made by another party.
out_of_scope: Attributes, state and lifecycle of the subject entity itself, which belong to the host model the mixin attaches to.
Design and minting of identifier schemes: syntax, check digits, allocation ranges and endpoint identifier schemes.
Execution of record-linkage or entity-resolution matching algorithms; this model records the resulting assertion and its justification, not the matcher runtime.
Runtime policy evaluation, authorization decisions and enforcement; only the policy reference and subject-specific binding parameters are carried.
Audit-trail record storage, immutability and retention execution; only the returned audit reference is stored.
Survivorship and golden-record attribute-merge rules for master data management.
Authoring of concept-scheme hierarchies (broader/narrower within a single scheme) and terminology curation.
Operation of HTTP servers, DNS, CDNs or proxies that execute a redirect projection emitted by this model.
Cryptographic key management, signing services and signature verification infrastructure.

boundary_notes.distinction: That model defines how identifiers are formed, minted and resolved, including endpoint identifier schemes. WM-XCT-036 consumes identifiers as opaque references and only asserts equivalence between them; it emits a redirect rule set but defines no endpoint scheme and serves no request.

The engine computes candidate matches and similarity scores. WM-XCT-036 stores the decision, its justification, the tool and version that produced it, and the confidence value; it does not execute or tune matching.

WM-XCT-036 carries a policy reference and alias-specific binding parameters (for example, that a re-identifying alias inherits the higher sensitivity class). Evaluation, decision and enforcement remain wholly with the referenced model.

WM-XCT-036 emits change events and stores the audit reference returned to it. Audit-record lifecycle, immutability guarantees and retention execution belong to the audit model and are not reproduced here.

SKOS mapping properties relate concepts across concept schemes and do not entail individual identity; skos:exactMatch is transitive and symmetric but is not owl:sameAs. WM-XCT-036 asserts identity of subjects and treats SKOS predicates as a bound export vocabulary, never as an equivalent semantics.

PROV-O terms are used as alignment for attributing an assertion to an agent and an activity. Activity, agent and qualified-influence lifecycles are owned by the provenance model; prov:alternateOf in particular is weaker than identity and is never treated as an alias.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Serialization and transport standards (JSON-LD, CSVW, HTTP, document stores)
boundary_notes.distinction: These are projections of the alias set, not its semantics. A feature that exists only in one serialization is a defect to be promoted into the format-neutral record or removed.

Generic cross-cutting reference and identity machinery is inherited from the parent registry entry. WM-XCT-036 specializes it only for equivalence assertion, and does not restate generic identity, authority or conflict machinery that the parent already carries.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Normative mapping vocabulary (S38-S46): exactMatch is symmetric and transitive and a sub-property of closeMatch, and is disjoint with broadMatch and relatedMatch. Grounds the graded-match binding and its prohibited combinations.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Mapping to RDF Graphs (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Defines the bidirectional mapping between the SameIndividual axiom and owl:sameAs triples, grounding the strict-identity export binding and its entailment consequences.

sources.title: RDF Dataset Canonicalization (RDFC-1.0)
sources.relevance: Canonical N-Quads form with deterministic blank-node labels; two datasets share a canonical form iff isomorphic. Grounds canonicalization and digest rules for RDF projections.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Requires seconds in partial-time and an explicit time-offset of Z or a numeric offset; defines -00:00 as 'local offset unknown', distinct from Z. Grounds the timestamp rule.

sources.title: RFC 9562: Universally Unique IDentifiers (UUIDs)
sources.relevance: Obsoletes RFC 4122; specifies UUIDv4 for unpredictability and UUIDv7 for time-ordered keys, and the canonical hex-and-dash form. Grounds the third identity tier.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Normative 3xx semantics: 301/308 assert a new permanent URI, 302/307 are temporary, 303 points to a different resource. Grounds the redirect projection binding and the prohibition on projecting graded matches as permanent redirects.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Attribution, derivation and generation-time terms for assertion provenance; prov:alternateOf explicitly denotes different aspects of a thing without identity, which is the counterexample separating provenance alternation from aliasing.

sources.title: RFC 6902: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Patch
sources.relevance: Ordered, atomic operation sequence with a test operation; a failed operation means no operation is applied. Grounds the patch rules and the base-edition digest guard.

sources.title: JSON-LD 1.1: A JSON-based Serialization for Linked Data
sources.relevance: Context-driven term-to-IRI expansion and compaction, and blank-node identifier handling. Grounds deterministic prefix expansion in JSON projections and known round-trip caveats.

sources.title: Controlled Identifiers v1.0
sources.relevance: Defines alsoKnownAs for asserting that identifiers refer to the same subject, and states it is best practice not to treat them as equivalent without a reciprocating assertion, and that the assertion itself is not proof. Grounds reciprocity controls.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Separates a dataset from its distributions in multiple serializations and formats, and defines version, previousVersion and hasCurrentVersion. Grounds treating storage/interface bindings as distributions of one format-neutral alias set.

sources.title: A Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM) - Data Model
sources.relevance: Mandatory subject_id, predicate_id, object_id and mapping_justification; curie_map with CURIEs that MUST resolve without external resources; propagatable set-level slots; mapping_cardinality and predicate_modifier. Grounds the irreducible record and prefix governance.

sources.title: Generating RDF from Tabular Data on the Web
sources.relevance: Minimal mode retains only cell information and strips row/table framing; a separate metadata document is needed to preserve subject URIs, datatypes and relations. Grounds documented loss in tabular projections.

sources.title: Best Practice Recipes for Publishing RDF Vocabularies
sources.relevance: States the namespace chosen must be a Web address to which the publisher has write access, and specifies hash vs slash namespaces, 303 See Other for slash namespaces and content negotiation. Grounds namespace ownership and resolution layout.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
sources.relevance: MAJOR for incompatible changes, MINOR for backward-compatible additions, PATCH for fixes, and the rule that a released version's contents MUST NOT be modified. Grounds compatibility and edition-immutability rules.

sources.title: AGENTS.md - an open format for guiding coding agents
sources.version_or_date: Open format, no versioned specification, accessed 4 September 2026
sources.relevance: Establishes AGENTS.md as a vendor-neutral Markdown orientation file placed at the root, with nested files where the nearest file wins and no required fields of its own. Grounds the bootstrap contract's placement and read-order rules; the six required fields are a Vercy contract layered on top.

sources.title: When owl:sameAs Isn't the Same: An Analysis of Identity in Linked Data
sources.organization: Halpin, Hayes, McCusker, McGuinness and Thompson (ISWC 2010, Springer)
sources.relevance: Documents systematic misuse of owl:sameAs in published Linked Data and argues it encodes one point on a similarity scale that is often too strong. Used only to identify the over-strengthening failure mode, not to define semantics.

sources.title: SSSOM/TSV Serialisation
sources.relevance: Embedded YAML metadata block prefixed with '#' versus an external .sssom.yml file, fixed column order, pipe-separated multi-valued slots with escaping, mandatory slot condensation, and the rule that implementations not supporting non-standard slots MUST discard unknown keys and columns on read.

sources.title: SSSOM Support Functions: Hashing Mapping Records
sources.relevance: Defines a canonical S-expression over all Mapping slots except record_id and mapping_cardinality, with float truncation to three fractional digits and FNV-1a 64-bit hashing, and states equal hashes make records only 'highly likely' identical. Grounds the digest-is-not-identity rule.

bundles.name: Representation, Projection and Interoperability
bundles.description: How one format-neutral alias set is expressed across storage bindings, interfaces and external equivalence vocabularies, and how every loss, weakening and unsupported relation kind incurred by each expression is declared before publication.
bundles.rationale: DCAT separates a dataset from its distributions, and SSSOM mandates only one serialization while permitting implementations to discard unknown slots on read; CSVW minimal mode strips structural framing. Every published form is therefore a lossy or lossless distribution whose fidelity must be measured, not assumed, and external vocabularies (SKOS, OWL 2, alsoKnownAs) carry different and partly incompatible strengths.

layers.name: Storage and Interface Projection Neutrality
layers.description: Declares each supported storage and interface binding as a distribution of the same format-neutral alias set, states what each can carry, and maintains an evidence-backed register of what each loses on a write-then-read cycle.

findings.name: Storage and Interface Projection Capability Matrix
findings.description: A per-projection capability declaration covering Git-tracked file trees, MCP server resources, document-store collections, RDF graphs, tabular exports and HTTP APIs. For each projection it states which alias features are carried natively, which require an accompanying metadata document, which are unsupported, and which single projection is normative when two disagree. The matrix exists because a projection is a distribution of the alias set, never a variant of its meaning.

questions.text: Which storage and interface projections are declared conformant for this alias set, and which alias features can each carry natively?
answer_data: Projection identifier and binding kind (file tree, MCP resource, document collection, RDF graph, tabular export, HTTP API)
Per-feature capability flag: native, requires-companion-metadata, or unsupported
Declared conformance level and the schema version the projection is pinned to

questions.text: Which accompanying metadata document must travel with a projection that cannot embed alias-set metadata inline?
answer_data: Metadata embedding mode: embedded block or external document
Reference to the external metadata document and its edition
Binding rule stating that the projection is invalid when read without its companion metadata

questions.text: Which projection is normative when two projections of the same alias set disagree?
answer_data: Designated normative projection identifier
Ordered precedence list for the remaining projections
Divergence handling rule and the defect class raised on disagreement

questions.text: What conformance evidence shows that a projection preserves the alias features it claims to carry?
answer_data: Reference to the conformance test suite and the corpus edition used
Test run outcome per declared feature, with pass, fail or waived status
RFC 3339 timestamp of the run and the tool plus version that produced it

data_elements.name: Projection descriptor
data_elements.description: Identifies one declared storage or interface binding of the alias set, including its binding kind and the schema version it is pinned to.

data_elements.name: Feature capability flag
data_elements.description: Per alias feature and per projection, whether the feature is carried natively, requires a companion metadata document, or is unsupported.

data_elements.name: Normative projection designation
data_elements.description: The single projection that resolves disagreement between distributions of the same alias set, plus the precedence order for the rest.

artifacts.name: Projection capability matrix
artifacts.description: Machine-readable matrix of alias features against declared projections, with capability flags, companion-metadata requirements, precedence order and the pinned schema version.
media_or_form: Structured table serialized in any supported projection
Distribution description attached to the alias-set catalogue record
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI in a namespace the owner package controls; no master-system identifier exists for this artifact, so tier two of the identity priority applies. The matrix filename and schema version are never its identity.

findings.name: Round-Trip and Information-Loss Register
findings.description: An evidence-backed inventory of every information loss, semantic weakening, unsupported relation kind and round-trip limitation observed when an alias set is written to and re-read from each declared projection. Each entry names the affected feature, the projection, whether the loss is detectable by the reader, and the compensating carrier if one exists. Publication of a projection is blocked until its losses are declared here.

questions.text: Which alias features are lost or silently weakened on each declared write-then-read cycle?
answer_data: Lost or weakened feature name and the projection that causes it
Loss class: dropped, coerced, flattened, reordered, or semantically weakened
Detectability flag stating whether a reader can notice the loss without the source
Compensating carrier reference, or an explicit statement that none exists

questions.text: What round-trip test corpus and result set demonstrate that the loss inventory is current?
answer_data: Test corpus reference and edition serial
Result set with per-case source and re-read canonical digests
RFC 3339 run timestamp and the implementation plus version under test

questions.text: What must an implementation do when it encounters a non-standard slot or an unsupported relation kind it cannot represent?
answer_data: Required behaviour: discard-and-report, refuse, or route to an extension carrier
The loss-register entry the discard must be recorded against
Notice returned to the caller naming the discarded keys or columns

questions.text: On what basis may a lossy projection still be accepted for publication rather than rejected?
answer_data: Acceptance criteria and the severity threshold applied
Approving role and the reference to the approval record
Mitigation or companion-metadata requirement attached to the acceptance

data_elements.name: Loss register entry
data_elements.description: One declared information loss or semantic weakening, bound to a feature, a projection, a loss class and a detectability flag.

data_elements.name: Round-trip fidelity verdict
data_elements.description: Result of comparing the canonical form of a source alias set with the canonical form of the same set after a write-then-read cycle through a projection.

data_elements.name: Compensating carrier reference
data_elements.description: The companion metadata document, extension slot or annotation that preserves a feature the projection cannot carry natively.

artifacts.name: Round-trip loss register
artifacts.description: Published register of declared losses, weakenings and unsupported relation kinds per projection, with detectability and compensating carriers.
media_or_form: Structured register serialized in any supported projection
Human-readable release note derived from the same register
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI for the register plus an opaque monotonic edition sequence assigned by the owner package; the sequence is not a date and the register digest is not its identity.

artifacts.name: Round-trip conformance corpus
artifacts.description: Fixture alias sets exercising every declared feature, including graded matches, negated assertions, multi-valued slots, non-ASCII labels, extension slots and blank-node-bearing RDF fragments, with expected canonical forms.
media_or_form: Fixture collection with expected canonical forms and digests
Test manifest binding each fixture to the features it exercises
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus an opaque monotonic edition sequence; individual fixtures carry Dimension-assigned UUIDs only where no governed IRI is warranted.

layers.name: External Predicate Binding and Semantic Fidelity
layers.description: Binds internal alias strength to predicates in external equivalence vocabularies, records the downgrade or refusal applied when the target cannot carry a feature, and controls the entailment and reciprocity risks that binding creates.

findings.name: External Equivalence Predicate Binding Profile
findings.description: The declared mapping from each internal alias strength and kind to a predicate in a target vocabulary — owl:sameAs for strict individual identity, skos:exactMatch or skos:closeMatch for graded concept-level matches, alsoKnownAs for unverified subject-level claims, and an SSSOM predicate_id with an optional predicate_modifier for interchange — together with the exact downgrade recorded whenever the target predicate is weaker or the alias feature is inexpressible. Bindings are alignments, not conformance claims.

questions.text: Which target-vocabulary predicate is bound to each internal alias strength, and how is negation expressed?
answer_data: Internal alias strength or kind
Bound target predicate IRI and target vocabulary version
Negation or modifier term used to express an explicit non-equivalence

questions.text: Which predicate combinations are prohibited because the target vocabulary declares them disjoint?
answer_data: Prohibited predicate pair and the integrity condition that forbids it
Detection rule applied before export
Required resolution: withhold, re-classify, or split the assertion

questions.text: How is an alias feature the target vocabulary cannot express carried alongside the exported statement?
answer_data: Inexpressible feature name, for example confidence, validity interval or asserting authority
Carriage mechanism: reified annotation, companion mapping-set metadata, or omission
Loss-register entry the omission is recorded against

questions.text: Who may approve a binding that would export an assertion under a stronger predicate than the internal strength?
answer_data: Approving role and the scope of the delegation
Reference to the approval record and its RFC 3339 decision time
Default outcome when no approval exists, namely refusal to export

data_elements.name: Predicate binding entry
data_elements.description: One declared correspondence between an internal alias strength and a target-vocabulary predicate, with the target vocabulary version.

data_elements.name: Semantic downgrade note
data_elements.description: Records that an exported statement is weaker than the internal assertion, or that a feature was dropped, with the reason and the affected feature.

data_elements.name: Predicate modifier
data_elements.description: Qualifier that negates or otherwise conditions the bound predicate, so that an explicit non-equivalence is not exported as an equivalence.

artifacts.name: Predicate binding profile
artifacts.description: Declarative profile binding internal alias strengths to target-vocabulary predicates, with disjointness prohibitions, downgrade table and inexpressible-feature carriage rules.
media_or_form: Declarative mapping profile in any supported projection
Context or vocabulary-alignment document consumable by an export tool
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI in the owner package's namespace plus an opaque monotonic edition sequence; target vocabulary versions are referenced, never re-minted.

findings.name: Entailment and Reciprocity Risk Controls
findings.description: The guard settings that prevent an export from creating inference the alias record does not support. owl:sameAs licenses full substitution and unlimited closure; skos:exactMatch is symmetric and transitive within the mapping vocabulary but entails no individual identity; alsoKnownAs asserts nothing verified in the absence of a reciprocating assertion in the other subject's document. These controls set the thresholds and refusal conditions applied at export time and the invalidation signal sent when a previously exported equivalence is retracted.

questions.text: Which entailment closure does each bound predicate license in the consuming system?
answer_data: Bound predicate and the closure properties it carries: symmetry, transitivity, substitution
Maximum cluster size or closure depth accepted before human review
Statement of what the internal assertion does and does not warrant

questions.text: What reciprocity evidence is required before an incoming third-party equivalence claim may be treated as equivalence?
answer_data: Reciprocity status: reciprocated, unreciprocated, or unverifiable
Reference to the reciprocating document and its retrieval time
Downgraded internal strength applied while reciprocity is pending

questions.text: What guard prevents a graded or low-confidence alias from being emitted under a strict identity predicate?
answer_data: Minimum confidence and justification class required for a strict-identity export
Guard outcome: emit, downgrade, or withhold
Record of every withheld alias with the reason code

questions.text: How is a consumer of a previously exported equivalence notified when that equivalence is retracted or contested?
answer_data: Invalidation signal kind and the projections it must be issued to
Reference to the superseding or retracting record and its event time
Cache and redirect regeneration obligation triggered by the signal

data_elements.name: Closure licence declaration
data_elements.description: Per bound predicate, the entailment closure the consuming system is expected to perform and the limit beyond which review is required.

data_elements.name: Reciprocity status
data_elements.description: Whether an equivalence claim made about a subject is reciprocated in the counterpart's own controlling document, and when that was checked.

data_elements.name: Export guard outcome
data_elements.description: The emit, downgrade or withhold decision applied to a single alias at export time, with its reason code.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are inline threshold and guard parameters evaluated per export request against the predicate binding profile; they are decision inputs, not a separately published document. Emitting them as their own artifact would create a second copy that drifts from the binding profile it must be read with, and would misrepresent ownership: the guard is applied by the referenced export and validation runtime, which owns execution, while this model owns only the parameter values and the recorded outcome.

layers.name: Resolution and Redirect Projection
layers.description: How an alias set is expressed as resolvable web behaviour — status-code binding, Location targets, namespace layout and cache validity — while the service that executes the behaviour remains outside this model.

findings.name: Redirect and Resolution Projection Binding
findings.description: Binds alias status to HTTP behaviour: a superseded identifier whose canonical replacement is settled maps to a permanent redirect (301 or 308), a provisional or under-review equivalence maps to a temporary redirect (302 or 307), and a slash-namespace term that denotes a non-information resource is served with 303 See Other. Graded matches are never projected as permanent redirects. This model emits a server-agnostic redirect rule set and cache directives; the HTTP service that executes them is a referenced neighbour.

questions.text: Which HTTP status class is bound to each alias status, and what is the Location target?
answer_data: Alias status and the bound status code with its permanence semantics
Location target IRI, drawn from the canonical-identifier selection
Explicit exclusion list of alias strengths that must not be redirected at all

questions.text: Who holds write authority over the namespace whose URIs a redirect projection claims to govern?
answer_data: Namespace stem and the authority holding write access to it
Evidence of delegation where the authority is not the owner package
Refusal rule for emitting redirects into a namespace the owner package does not control

questions.text: What does this model emit for redirect behaviour, and which system actually performs the redirect?
answer_data: Emitted rule-set form and its projection binding
Named executing system or service class, held as a reference
Statement that request handling, content negotiation execution and logging are outside this model

questions.text: How long may a redirect projection be cached, and when must it be regenerated after an alias change?
answer_data: Cache directive and maximum validity period per status class
Regeneration trigger events, including retraction and canonical-identifier change
RFC 3339 generation time of the rule set and the alias-set edition it was derived from

data_elements.name: Redirect rule
data_elements.description: One server-agnostic rule binding a source identifier to a target IRI and an HTTP status class, with its permanence semantics.

data_elements.name: Namespace write authority
data_elements.description: The party holding write access to the namespace stem for which redirect or canonical-identifier claims are published.

data_elements.name: Cache validity directive
data_elements.description: Maximum caching period for a redirect rule and the events that force regeneration.

artifacts.name: Redirect projection rule set
artifacts.description: Server-agnostic set of source-to-target redirect rules with bound status classes, cache directives and content-negotiation preferences, derived from a named alias-set edition and intended for execution by an external HTTP service.
media_or_form: Declarative rule set in any supported projection, translatable to a specific server configuration
Accompanying derivation record naming the source alias-set edition and its digest
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus an opaque monotonic edition sequence; the rule set is never identified by the digest of its generated server configuration or by the generation timestamp.

bundles.name: Canonical Identity, Namespace and Change Control
bundles.description: The governance controls that keep an alias set stable and comparable over time: who owns the namespaces and prefixes, what the canonical schema and version promise, how records are identified and timed, and how canonical form and digests are computed and verified.
bundles.rationale: SSSOM requires every compact identifier to expand without external lookup; the W3C vocabulary-publishing recipes require write authority over the namespace published; Semantic Versioning forbids mutating a released version; RFC 3339, RFC 9562 and the SSSOM hashing rules together fix how time, identity and integrity are recorded. Without these, two readers of the same alias set can legitimately disagree about what it says.

layers.name: Namespace Ownership and Canonical Schema Versioning
layers.description: Declares which namespaces the owner package controls, how compact identifiers expand deterministically, what canonical schema and version an alias set claims, and what compatibility a consumer may rely on.

findings.name: Namespace Ownership and Prefix Expansion Governance
findings.description: Declares the namespaces the owner package owns outright versus those it merely references under another authority's control, and publishes the prefix-to-IRI map that lets every compact identifier in an alias set expand to a full IRI without consulting any external resource. Covers collision handling when two declarations bind one prefix to different stems, and pins which prefix-map edition was in force when a record was written.

questions.text: Which namespaces does the adopting Dimension own outright, and which are referenced under another authority?
answer_data: Namespace stem and ownership class: owned, delegated, or referenced
Controlling authority reference for each referenced stem
Permitted operations per class, in particular the prohibition on redefining referenced stems

questions.text: How is every compact identifier in an alias set expanded to a full IRI without consulting an external registry?
answer_data: Prefix-to-IRI stem declarations bundled with or referenced by the alias set
Expansion algorithm and the rule that unresolvable prefixes reject the record
Round-trip requirement that compaction of an expanded IRI returns the original compact form

questions.text: What happens when two prefix declarations bind the same prefix to different IRI stems?
answer_data: Collision detection point: authoring, ingest, or export
Resolution rule and precedence between set-level and external declarations
Rejection or quarantine outcome and the defect record raised

questions.text: Which prefix-map edition was in force when a given alias record was written?
answer_data: Prefix-map edition serial pinned by the record or its set
Digest of the pinned prefix-map edition
Re-expansion obligation when a later edition changes a stem

data_elements.name: Namespace ownership declaration
data_elements.description: One namespace stem with its ownership class and, where not owned, the controlling authority reference.

data_elements.name: Prefix binding
data_elements.description: A compact-identifier prefix bound to a full IRI stem, sufficient for unambiguous expansion without external lookup.

data_elements.name: Prefix map edition pin
data_elements.description: The prefix-map edition serial and digest that an alias record or set was authored against.

artifacts.name: Prefix and namespace map
artifacts.description: Published prefix-to-IRI stem map with ownership classes, collision precedence and deprecation markers, sufficient on its own to expand every compact identifier in the alias sets that pin it.
media_or_form: Prefix map serialized in any supported projection
Context document consumable by a linked-data processor
Namespace document served from the owned stem
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI in an owned namespace plus an opaque monotonic edition sequence; the map is never identified by its publication date or by the digest of its serialized form.

findings.name: Canonical Schema, Versioning and Compatibility Promise
findings.description: The canonical schema an alias record and alias set are validated against, the version identifier they declare, which changes count as breaking for a consumer, how a released edition is superseded without being mutated, and what a consumer must do when it meets a version it does not fully recognise. This is the promise that makes safe evolution possible without renegotiating every consumer.

questions.text: Which canonical schema and version does an alias set declare, and where is that schema dereferenced?
answer_data: Canonical schema reference and its dereferenceable location
Declared version identifier in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH form
Validation profile applied, and whether it is strict or lenient about unknown slots

questions.text: Which schema changes are breaking for a consumer of an exported alias set?
answer_data: Change class: additive, restrictive, renaming, semantic re-binding, or removal
Breaking or non-breaking verdict with the version increment it forces
Consumer impact statement and any migration path offered

questions.text: How is a released schema or alias-set edition superseded without mutating what was already published?
answer_data: New edition serial and its supersession pointer to the prior edition
Immutability assertion for the prior edition and its digest
Support window during which the superseded edition remains dereferenceable

questions.text: What must a consumer do when it reads a minor version whose additions it does not recognise?
answer_data: Required behaviour within a major line: ignore unknown slots rather than fail
Obligation to report discarded slots so the loss register stays accurate
Failure condition that does justify rejection, namely an unrecognised major version

data_elements.name: Canonical schema reference
data_elements.description: Dereferenceable pointer to the schema an alias record or set is validated against, with its declared version.

data_elements.name: Compatibility verdict
data_elements.description: Whether a proposed change is breaking for consumers, and the version increment it therefore requires.

data_elements.name: Edition supersession pointer
data_elements.description: Reference from a new edition to the edition it supersedes, preserving the prior edition unmodified.

artifacts.name: Canonical alias-set schema
artifacts.description: The authoritative, dereferenceable schema defining alias record and alias-set slots, cardinalities, value kinds and validation constraints, independent of any serialization.
media_or_form: Schema document dereferenceable from an owned namespace
Projection-specific schema bindings generated from it and marked as derived
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI for the schema plus a declared semantic version; version strings and file names locate an edition but never constitute the schema's identity.

artifacts.name: Schema and edition change log
artifacts.description: Ordered record of every edition, the patch document that produced it, its compatibility verdict, its base and resulting digests, and its supersession pointer.
media_or_form: Ordered change record in any supported projection
Patch series with base-digest test operations
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus an opaque monotonic edition sequence; the sequence carries order only and never encodes the change date.

layers.name: Record Identity, Time Discipline and Integrity
layers.description: Fixes how alias records are identified, how their times are recorded and distinguished, how their canonical form is computed and how integrity is verified without confusing a digest with an identifier.

findings.name: Alias Record Identity and Time Discipline
findings.description: Applies the identity priority to alias records and sets — an authoritative master-system identifier where one exists, otherwise a governed IRI in a controlled namespace, otherwise a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID — and forbids dates, version strings, digests, file names and projection-local surrogate keys from acting as identity. Separately fixes the time discipline: the time the equivalence was asserted by its authority, the time this model first observed it, and the time it was written into a projection are three distinct values recorded whenever they differ.

questions.text: Which identifier is authoritative for an alias record when a master system already assigns one?
answer_data: Master-system identifier value and the system of record that assigns it
Identity tier actually applied, with the reason a lower tier was needed if so
Immutability assertion binding that identifier to the record for its lifetime

questions.text: How are the time an equivalence was asserted, first observed and written recorded distinctly?
answer_data: Assertion event time as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset
Observation time recorded when this model first saw the assertion
Ingestion time recorded when the record was written into a projection

questions.text: Why may a content digest, file name or version string never be promoted to a record identifier?
answer_data: Statement that equal digests establish only high likelihood of identical content, not identity of records
Statement that identity fields are excluded from the canonical form, so a digest cannot be self-referential
Rejection rule applied when a projection proposes a digest or path as a key

questions.text: Which clock and offset applied when a timestamp was recorded, and was the local offset known?
answer_data: Recorded numeric offset or Z, and the source of the clock
Use of the minus-zero-zero offset convention where the instant is known in UTC but the local offset is not
Agent or tool reference that generated the timestamp

data_elements.name: Alias record identifier
data_elements.description: The single identifier of an alias record or set, assigned by the identity priority and immutable thereafter.

data_elements.name: Assertion event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 date-time, with seconds and an explicit offset, at which the asserting authority made or retracted the equivalence claim.

data_elements.name: Observation and ingestion times
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 date-times at which this model first observed the assertion and at which the record was written into a projection, recorded separately from event time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity and time are field-level constraints that must hold inside every alias record in every projection; they are enforced by the canonical schema and the validation profile that already exist as artifacts. Publishing them separately would duplicate the schema and create a second source of truth for constraints that must be checked in-band at create and patch time, and it would invite drift between the published document and the rules actually applied.

findings.name: Canonical Form, Digest and Integrity Verification
findings.description: Defines the deterministic canonical form used for comparison, diffing, digesting and signing. Two regimes apply and are declared explicitly rather than merged: RDF projections are canonicalized to canonical N-Quads with deterministic blank-node labels, where two datasets share a canonical form if and only if they are isomorphic; slot-record projections are canonicalized by propagating set-level slots, ordering slots by the schema's slot order, sorting multi-valued slots, truncating floating-point confidence, and excluding identity and computed-cardinality fields. Digests verify integrity and detect drift only.

questions.text: What is the canonical form of an alias record, and which fields are excluded from it?
answer_data: Ordered normalization steps: slot propagation, slot ordering, multi-value sorting, numeric truncation, encoding
Excluded fields, specifically the record identity field and any computed cardinality field
Statement of the canonicalization regime that applies to the projection at hand

questions.text: Which digest algorithm and encoding are used, and what collision assumption is stated alongside them?
answer_data: Algorithm identifier and output encoding
Stated collision assumption and the permitted uses of the digest
Prohibited uses, in particular use as an identifier or as proof of record identity

questions.text: How does a consumer verify that a received alias set matches the published edition byte for byte?
answer_data: Published integrity manifest entry for the edition, with its digest and algorithm
Verification procedure the consumer runs after canonicalization
Mismatch handling: reject, quarantine, and the defect record raised

questions.text: How is canonical form computed for a graph projection that contains unlabelled nodes?
answer_data: Canonicalization algorithm applied and the deterministic labels it assigns
Isomorphism guarantee and its limits
Statement that digests from the graph regime and the slot-record regime are not comparable

data_elements.name: Canonicalization profile
data_elements.description: The named regime and ordered normalization steps applied before any digest, diff or signature is computed for a given projection.

data_elements.name: Edition digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the canonical form of one published edition, with its algorithm and encoding, used solely for integrity and drift detection.

data_elements.name: Integrity verification verdict
data_elements.description: Outcome of comparing a received edition's recomputed digest with the published manifest entry.

artifacts.name: Canonicalization profile specification
artifacts.description: Declares each canonicalization regime, its ordered normalization steps, excluded fields, numeric truncation rule and encoding, and states which regime applies to which projection.
media_or_form: Specification document dereferenceable from an owned namespace
Machine-readable profile consumable by a canonicalization implementation
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus a declared semantic version; the profile is never identified by the digest it produces.

artifacts.name: Integrity manifest
artifacts.description: Per-edition list of canonical-form digests with algorithm and encoding identifiers, published alongside each alias-set edition for verification.
media_or_form: Manifest in any supported projection, paired with the edition it covers
Detached verification record referenced by the edition's catalogue entry
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus an opaque monotonic edition sequence matching the edition it covers; the manifest's own digest is not its identity.

functions.name: Project alias set into a declared binding
functions.description: Renders the format-neutral alias set into one declared storage or interface projection, applying the projection capability matrix, the pinned prefix map and the predicate binding profile, and returning every downgrade and omission applied.

Projection descriptor and capability flags
Prefix map edition pin
Predicate binding profile edition
outputs: Projection artifact for the target binding
Applied-loss report referencing loss register entries
Companion metadata document where the projection cannot embed set metadata
preconditions: The projection is declared conformant for the alias set's schema version
Every compact identifier expands unambiguously against the pinned prefix map
All losses the projection will cause are already declared in the loss register
effects: Emits a distribution of the alias set without altering the format-neutral record
Records each applied downgrade and each discarded non-standard slot against its loss-register entry

functions.name: Verify projection round-trip fidelity
functions.description: Writes a corpus alias set through a projection, reads it back, canonicalizes both sides and reports which declared features survived, which were lost and which losses are undeclared.

Projection descriptor and implementation under test
Canonicalization profile

Delta against the current loss register
Blocking defect list for undeclared losses

The corpus edition covers every feature the projection claims to carry

Blocks publication of the projection while any undeclared loss remains open

Target vocabulary identifier and version
Predicate binding profile and export guard parameters

Semantic downgrade note, or a refusal reason code
List of features that cannot be carried and their carriage decision

No prohibited predicate pair is created by the binding
Any strengthening binding carries a valid approval reference

Withholds the alias from export when no sufficiently weak predicate exists

functions.name: Expand and compact identifiers deterministically
functions.description: Expands a compact identifier to a full IRI, or compacts a full IRI, using only the pinned prefix map edition, and raises an error rather than guessing when a prefix is undeclared or ambiguous.
inputs: Compact identifier or full IRI
Prefix map edition pin and its digest
outputs: Full IRI or compact identifier
Ambiguity or undeclared-prefix error with the offending prefix

No prefix in the map binds to more than one stem

functions.name: Compute canonical form and edition digest
functions.description: Applies the canonicalization regime appropriate to the projection, produces the canonical byte sequence and computes the edition digest with a named algorithm and encoding.
inputs: Alias record or alias-set edition
Canonicalization profile and regime selector
Digest algorithm and encoding identifiers

Edition digest with algorithm and encoding identifiers
List of fields excluded from the canonical form

Identity and computed-cardinality fields are declared excluded

Never assigns or derives a record identifier from the digest

functions.name: Emit a redirect projection rule set
functions.description: Derives a server-agnostic redirect rule set from an alias-set edition, binding alias status to a permanent, temporary or see-other status class and setting cache directives, for execution by an external HTTP service.

Namespace write-authority declarations

Derivation record naming the source edition and its digest

Marks previously emitted rule sets for regeneration when the source edition is superseded

functions.name: Apply a versioned patch to an alias-set edition

Ordered patch document beginning with a base-digest test operation
Target schema version

Compatibility verdict and required version increment
Change-log entry linking base and result

The patch does not attempt to modify an already released edition

Applies all operations or none, and appends the outcome to the change log

functions.description: Assigns the identifier for a new alias record or set by walking the identity priority in order and recording which tier was used and why any higher tier was unavailable.

Governed namespace stem available to the owner package
Minting context indicating whether time-ordered or unpredictable identifiers are required

Justification when a lower tier was used
Rejection when a date, digest, version string or file path was proposed as identity

Storage binding descriptor, including MCP server or collection descriptors
Interface binding descriptor and process catalogue

Resolution report confirming each declared link dereferences

The storage binding names the server or collection descriptor rather than a filesystem path when records are not file-held
